overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficiently detailed minutes for its December 8, 2020 meeting; the notice was sufficiently specific, no intentional violation was found, and the earth-removal allegation was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the minutes of the December 8, 2020 meeting were insufficiently detailed, missing the zoning discussion beyond a single motion.
allegations.key_passage: Because the meeting minutes do not capture the Town Planner’s presentation, nor any of the Board’s discussion leading up to the vote, we find that the minutes of the December 8 meeting are insufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the Board's insufficient minutes were an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We find no other evidence of an intentional violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the December 8, 2020 meeting notice's 'possible zoning amendments' topic was not sufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the notice for the Board’s December 8 meeting was sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board has not sufficiently discussed the Town's earth removal by-law during its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend the minutes of the December 8, 2020 meeting within 30 days of receipt of the determination to include a summary of the discussion of possible zoning amendments.
remedy_passage: We also order the Board to amend the minutes of its December 8, 2020, meeting within 30 days of receipt of this determination to include a summary of the discussion of possible zoning amendments that took place during the December 8 meeting.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
